recent.question: North Texas wins
recent.what_happened: North Texas won at Tulsa 45-38 in overtime on Oct 1, 2026, so the market resolved Yes. A game that went to overtime was close to a coin flip, and the result could easily have gone the other way.
recent.what_we_missed: Nothing decisive was missed. Our forecasts (0.43–0.47) were slightly under the market's 0.525. That small gap came from weighting Tulsa's home field, Baylor Hayes returning at quarterback, and UNT's injuries more heavily than UNT's top-10 offense and its recent wins in the series.
recent.lesson: In conference games that look like toss-ups, don't drift away from the market unless a specific fact justifies it. Here, our small lean toward Tulsa had no edge behind it.

suggested_change.change: Skip bets, or stay at the market price, when our probability is within about 5–7 points of the market and we can't name a specific piece of information the market lacks.

recent.question: Cleveland wins
recent.what_happened: Cleveland beat Pittsburgh 27-24 at home on Thursday Night Football. The Browns led 21-10 at halftime after a big second quarter, then held on in a three-point game.
recent.what_we_missed: Nothing decisive. The research forecast of 0.47 already sat above the market's 0.425 because of Cleveland's recent home wins over Pittsburgh and the Steelers' secondary injuries. A three-point result is essentially a coin flip.
recent.lesson: In close divisional home games, give real weight to the home-field record and opponent injuries over the market's lean. The research-informed forecast did this and was right to move toward Cleveland.

suggested_change.change: No process change needed. The forecast was well calibrated and the more likely side of a near-50/50 game happened not to be the one that won, so this outcome tells us little.

recent.question: Atlanta wins
recent.what_happened: Atlanta beat Philadelphia 6-2 at home in the winner-take-all Game 3 to win the Wild Card Series. Nola and Wheeler, who pitched together, gave up five runs on two home runs.
recent.what_we_missed: Philadelphia's 10-4 postseason record against Atlanta and its 1-3 record in elimination games are small samples from past seasons. They did not justify putting Atlanta 13 points below a market that had it at about 50%. The evidence that actually bears on this game favored Atlanta: home field, a 94-68 record against 88-74, a 9-4 head-to-head record this season, and a 66-43 run edge.
recent.lesson: In a single playoff game where the market is near 50/50, do not move far from it on postseason history between the franchises or other narrative stats. Weight current-season team strength and home field more heavily.

suggested_change.change: Limit how much small-sample historical or narrative base rates (franchise playoff records, all-time head-to-head) can move the forecast away from a liquid market price, for example to 5 points at most, unless current-season evidence points the same way.

recent.question: Darnell Washington: 1+ touchdowns
recent.what_happened: In the Week 4 TNF loss in Cleveland, Darnell Washington caught a 21-yard touchdown pass from Aaron Rodgers right after Rodgers took his fifth sack. The market resolved YES.
recent.what_we_missed: All of the research was about RB Jaylen Warren, not TE Darnell Washington. Nothing in it covered Washington's role, his red-zone usage, or how Cleveland defends tight ends, so the 0.29 rested on the wrong player's profile. That number was above the 0.125 market only by accident.
recent.lesson: Before using any fact, check that the player named in the research matches the player in the market title. Throw out evidence about a different player instead of treating it as a proxy.

suggested_change.change: Add an automatic check that blocks a forecast for a player prop when most of the research facts name a player other than the one in the question.

recent.question: Haiti wins
recent.what_happened: Haiti won 4-1 away in Santo Domingo. Wilson Isidor scored twice, Louicius Deedson and Yassin Fortune added one each, and Dorny Romero scored the Dominican Republic's only goal. The market resolved YES.
recent.what_we_missed: Our forecasts of 0.30–0.40 sat below the market's 0.485, mainly because we gave too much weight to home advantage and the Dominican Republic's 15-game unbeaten home run. We gave too little weight to Haiti being a 2026 World Cup side in strong form, led by Isidor. That home run was probably built against weaker opponents, and the Dominican Republic was new to League A and missing Edarlyn Reyes.
recent.lesson: When the market already prices a stronger away team as a slight favourite, don't move well below it because of a home streak unless you've checked who that streak was against.

suggested_change.change: Before using a team's home unbeaten streak to justify a price below the market, check how strong the opponents in that streak were and compare the two teams' recent tournament level, such as World Cup qualification or FIFA ranking.

recent.question: San Diego wins
recent.what_happened: San Diego won Game 2 of the NL Wild Card Series at Petco Park. Nick Pivetta allowed one run over 3 1/3 innings and left with the Padres up 2-1, and the bullpen held on. Sources disagree on Game 1: one search summary says San Diego won 8-0, but an SI URL says the Padres lost and faced elimination.
recent.what_we_missed: The forecaster never found the Game 1 result, even though the game ended hours before the judgment time. It also set its probability below the market's 56.5% despite reasons to favor San Diego: home field, Pivetta's 1.45 ERA since returning, and hints of a Gausman shoulder injury.
recent.lesson: In a near coin-flip game, don't go below the market's favorite unless you have specific evidence. Home field, a hot starter and a possibly injured opposing starter all pointed toward the market price or higher.

suggested_change.change: For multi-game playoff series, first look up the previous game's final score using box-score sources such as MLB.com Gameday or Baseball-Reference, and check whether announced starters are healthy before setting a probability.

recent_wins.question: Will Curaçao win on 2026-10-01?
recent_wins.what_happened: Curaçao beat Trinidad and Tobago 1-0 at Ergilio Hato on October 1, 2026. Juninho Bacuna scored the only goal in the 58th minute, so Curaçao won in regulation and the market resolved YES.
recent_wins.what_worked: The research raised the forecast from 0.35 (jev_alone) to 0.67, a little above the market's 0.605. It found strong recent evidence: Curaçao had won both group games and scored 10 goals, Trinidad and Tobago had 0 points and several key players out (Spicer, Sealy, Mitchell, James, Henry), Curaçao were unbeaten in the last four head-to-heads, and T&T had dropped points in their last four Nations League away games. The edge over the market was small, though, and a single-goal win could easily have been a draw that resolved NO. The direction was right, but this result proves little about the size o
recent_wins.lesson: When a home favorite has better recent form and the opponent is missing several confirmed starters, trust the team-news research over a prior that ignores context. But size a 6-point edge over the market modestly, because one goal decides many of these games.

suggested_change.change: When team-news sources disagree (here Wired868's injury list against an aggregator showing no T&T absences), have the researcher check the confirmed matchday squad or lineup before judging, so the edge rests on verified availability.

recent_wins.question: Will Norway win on 2026-10-01?
recent_wins.what_happened: Wales beat Norway 2-1 in Cardiff. Oscar Bobb put Norway ahead early, Daniel James equalised before half-time, and Neco Williams scored the winner from a free-kick soon after Torbjørn Heggem was sent off with a straight red. Norway did not win, so the market resolved No.
recent_wins.what_worked: The forecast gave Norway 0.37 while the market had them at 0.675, so it was right on the side it picked. But none of the researched facts supported it: Norway were the much higher-ranked team, Haaland was in form, and Wales had a long injury list, a winless run and no Nations League goals. Norway were leading until a red card changed the match, so the result came from a random event, not from anything the research found.
recent_wins.lesson: If our number is 30 points away from the market and none of our evidence points against the favourite, treat that as a sign we may have made an error, not as an edge, and check the inputs before betting big.

suggested_change.change: The 'rules' fact the forecaster was given was wrong: it said a draw or a cancellation resolves Yes, which is the wording of a draw market, while the real rules say only a Norway win resolves Yes. Add a check that the rules summary matches the question's YES condition before any forecast or bet goes ahead.

recent_wins.question: Will Bitcoin reach $87,500 in September?
recent_wins.what_happened: Bitcoin's September peak was about $87,397 on Sept 21, roughly $100 short of the $87,500 strike. It then slid to about $83,600–84,600 on Sept 30, so no Binance 1-minute high reached $87,500 and the market resolved NO.
recent_wins.what_worked: Very little of the 0.27 figure was earned. On the morning of the last day, BTC was about 1% below the reported monthly high, which came from an unnamed source and was not confirmed on Binance, and it needed to rise about 3.5–4.5% in roughly 15 hours. The market's 0.11 was closer to the truth, and leaning toward NO is the only part that held up. The real driver was a fact the research half-noticed: the stated high was already just under the strike. The research then compared prices to the wrong strike ($85,000).
recent_wins.lesson: When the question's strike sits just above a reported intraday high, check the high on the exact resolution venue (Binance BTC/USDT 1m) and price the time left, which here was under one day of normal volatility, instead of anchoring on how close the earlier high came.

suggested_change.change: Make researchers restate the question's exact strike and compare every price fact to it. In this case the facts were framed against $85,000 while the question asked about $87,500, which hid how far the price still had to rise.

recent_wins.question: Chicago WS wins
recent_wins.what_happened: The White Sox won Game 2 in Houston 7-3, helped by Chase Meidroth's three-run homer in the sixth. That swept the Wild Card Series, and they move on to face Cleveland in the ALDS.
recent_wins.what_worked: The research forecast (0.54) leaned against Houston's edge from Hunter Brown and home field. It gave weight to Burke's strong 2026 numbers against Houston (1.54 ERA), Chicago's better record and their Game 1 momentum, and it correctly threw out the misleading 'Astros 2-0' score, which was from a September regular-season game. But a single playoff game priced near 42-54% is close to a coin flip, so the win mostly came down to variance, not an edge.
recent_wins.lesson: For a single MLB game, only move away from the market when you have a concrete edge such as an injury or lineup news; 'team leads series 1-0' base rates describe the whole series and say little about the next game.

suggested_change.change: Cap stake size on single-game MLB markets when the forecast is within about 15 points of the market and no injury or lineup information has turned up that the market lacks.

recent_wins.question: Boston wins
recent_wins.what_happened: The Yankees beat the Red Sox 9-0 in Game 1 of the AL Wild Card Series at Yankee Stadium. Cam Schlittler struck out 10 over six shutout innings, and Payton Tolle gave up one run in 4⅔ innings before the Yankees pulled away against Boston's bullpen.
recent_wins.what_worked: The research turned up the lopsided starting-pitcher matchup (Schlittler's AL-leading 1.95 ERA and 215 ERA+ against a rookie), Boston's .579 OPS against the Yankees this season, and the Red Sox being outscored 34-15 at Yankee Stadium. Together these moved the forecast from 0.48 without research to 0.24, well below the market's 0.445. Even so, any single playoff game is noisy, and a 9-0 margin says more about the size of the edge than how sure we should have been.
recent_wins.lesson: In single playoff games with a big starting-pitcher gap and a strong head-to-head split, trust the matchup-specific numbers over a hazy 'road teams win Game 1' base rate recalled from memory.

suggested_change.change: Treat base-rate counts the research desk flags as 'from memory, source disagreed' as unverified. Check them against a source or leave them out, instead of letting them pull the forecast toward the underdog.

recent_wins.question: Minnesota wins
recent_wins.what_happened: The No. 8 seed Liberty beat the No. 1 seed Lynx 87-71 at Barclays Center on Sept 29. Minnesota never led, so New York swept the best-of-three series 2-0 and Minnesota was eliminated.
recent_wins.what_worked: Research pulled in the matchup-specific evidence: New York's 16-point road win in Game 1, its 3-1 edge in the 2026 head-to-head, Stewart's dominance, Miles's poor return from injury and the Lynx's 0-3 franchise record after losing Game 1. Together these moved the forecast from 0.49 without research to 0.23. The market stayed at 0.595 because it kept anchoring on Minnesota's 33-11 seed and 17-4 road record. Still, this was one playoff game, and a forecast of 0.23 means Minnesota wins about one time in four, so part of the good result is variance.
recent_wins.lesson: In a short playoff series between two strong teams, give more weight to direct head-to-head results and the most recent game than to regular-season record or seeding, especially when the lower seed has a strong record for its seed and a fresh blowout win.

suggested_change.change: Always collect head-to-head results from the current season and margins from earlier games in the series, and flag when the market's favorite is based mainly on seeding or overall record.

rules.rule: For short-window crypto price questions, record a spot price from the exchange and pair named in the resolution rules (e.g. Binance BTC/USDT), no more than an hour old at judgment time when the window closes within a day, and state its timestamp and age.

For crypto threshold questions, report the percent distance from current spot to the strike, the hours left in the window, and recent realized volatility over a similar span, noting whether the window falls on a usually quieter weekend.

Read the crypto resolution rules for the exact strike, venue and test (any touch in the window or a close at a set candle), restate that strike at the top of the research, and measure every price fact against it, not against a nearby round number.

Do not treat earlier-week touches of a level or prior days' closes as evidence about the current window; identify what drove those moves (e.g. a weekday bond-yield spike) and check whether that driver is still active now.

For short-horizon crypto questions, search same-day macro and geopolitical news (dollar, bond yields, oil, major policy statements) and report any specific catalyst with timestamps, or state plainly that none was found; label weeks-old news as stale background.

Before reporting a past high or low as reaching the strike, confirm it on the resolution venue's own candles (e.g. Binance 1-minute) and that it falls inside the question's window; label any report naming no exchange, or dated before the window opened, as unverified.
For single-match win questions, read the resolution rules to confirm whether only a win in regulation time counts, and state plainly that a draw would resolve No.

For match questions, report the current-season head-to-head with its game count, labeling samples under about 10 games as small and noting when sources disagree on the count, plus each side's dated, sourced suspensions, injuries and returns from injury.
Discard any search snippet claiming a match result that is undated or dated before kickoff; report a result only from sources published after the match was played.

For tennis 'completed match' questions, read which endings count as not completed (retirement, walkover), and report the historical share of matches finished through normal play at that tour level (WTA 125, ATP Challenger) as the starting reference.

For tennis completion questions, report as risk evidence only specific, dated news from the past week: an injury, a withdrawal, or a retirement at this event; label old retirements, back-to-back events or qualifying load, and a result not yet posted as weak context.

Just before a tennis match, check the tournament's latest order of play, draw updates and withdrawal lists for walkovers, late withdrawals or lucky-loser swaps, and report recent full matches each player finished (singles or doubles) as fitness evidence.

When a count question resolves on one named data provider, pull that provider's own trailing 2–4 week figures and write down its counting method (e.g. AIS-visible only) first; set aside other trackers' figures that count differently.

For single MLB games, report both confirmed starters' season ERA and ERA+ and recent starts, each team's season record, late-season form (record and offense since Sept 1) and home field; if it is a bullpen game, note that an opener's few innings carry little weight.

Take historical base-rate counts only from a cited source covering the current format (e.g. WNBA best-of-three since 2022); label any count recalled from memory, disputed between sources, or built on about a dozen cases as unverified.

For playoff series and games, state the current series score and what the trailing team must still win and where, report margins of earlier games in the series, and note when a team's standing rests mainly on seeding or overall record.

changes: Sharpened R1: spot price must be no more than an hour old when the window closes within a day, because a 4-hour-old price missed a decisive move (polymarket:4797724).
Sharpened R3: restate the exact strike and measure every price fact against it, because research was framed around $85,000 instead of the question's own strike (polymarket:4797724).
Sharpened R5: label weeks-old news as stale background rather than a catalyst, because weeks-old conflict news was treated as live risk (polymarket:4689727, polymarket:4797726).
Added evidence to R2 from polymarket:4689727 and polymarket:4797726, where distance, hours left and volatility were the deciding facts.

Added new crypto rule: confirm any reported high or low on the resolution venue's candles and inside the question's window, because unverified or pre-window reports ($2,807 ETH, $101 SOL) misled the research (polymarket:4844455, polymarket:4797726).
No rules made from kalshi:KXMLBGAME-26SEP301700CWSHOU-CWS, polymarket:4052418 or polymarket:4678632 (marked lucky), or from kalshi:KXMLBGAME-26SEP302200CHCSD-SD (marked unlucky).
Sharpened R7: head-to-head should be current-season, with game count, small-sample label and noted source disagreement, plus returns from injury (MLB CWS/HOU reviews, WNBA MIN game).
Added MLB single-game rule: starter ERA/ERA+, season record, late-season form, home field, and bullpen-game caveat (BOS/NYY worked; SD, CWS/HOU missed these).
Added general base-rate rule: cite a source for the current format and label memory-based, disputed or tiny-sample counts as unverified (BOS/NYY, WNBA series, SD, CWS).
Added playoff series rule: series score, what the trailing team needs and where, earlier game margins, and whether a team's standing rests on seeding (WNBA MIN reviews).
No rules made from the LV/IND WNBA and Trump 'Piggy' reviews because they are marked unlucky.

proposals.title: Shrink forecasts toward the market before computing edge
proposals.why: The market's Brier (0.123, 201 markets) beats every forecaster, and most of our losses came from bets where we disagreed with it most, such as long shots that went 1 for 21. A strategy option that blends the forecast with the market price (for example 50/50) before the edge check would bet only where a disagreement survives that discount. The forecasters themselves would still never see the price.
proposals.judge_by: Replay the blended rule on resolved markets that were judged after the code ships, and compare it with the unblended rule on the same markets. It succeeds if settled P&L per $100 is higher and it has fewer losing bets.

proposals.title: Score forecasters on 30c+ markets only
proposals.why: Since 2026-10-01 every strategy bets only at 30c or more, but the Brier table (market 0.114 vs our best 0.121) mixes in the long shots we no longer touch. We need to know whether any forecaster beats the price where we actually bet, matched market by market.
proposals.judge_by: The review data gains each source's Brier score next to the market's on the same resolved markets priced 30c or more. Success means Joey can see whether any source scores below the market there, which decides which challenger to start next.

proposals.title: Paired Brier scores and a calibration sanity check
proposals.why: Each source is scored on a different set of markets (Claude on 33, the market on 120), so 'Claude beats the market' can't be trusted. The calibration map has a=1.489, and its forecasts score worse than raw Jev (0.236 against 0.199), even though reviews blame Jev being overconfident. A=1.489 may be stretching forecasts further from 50/50 instead of pulling them back.
proposals.judge_by: Joey approves, and the next review shows Brier scores for each source against the market on the same resolved markets, plus the calibrated source's score on markets the map wasn't fitted to.
proposals.status_reason: approved by Joey 2026-10-02; needs a code session

proposals.title: Jev + research, picky
proposals.why: Bets main actually placed have lost $15 per $100 (7 settled), and Jev + research trails the market badly in crypto and economy. This tests whether requiring a 15% edge, and dropping both categories, turns research-driven bets profitable. It can run now, while main is locked until tomorrow.
proposals.judge_by: P&L per $100 staked is at or above zero, and above original's on the markets both bet over the same period.
proposals.status_reason: started automatically within the allowed bounds

proposals.title: Jev alone, bold: pickier, no crypto or economy
proposals.why: Jev alone scores worse than the market in every category, with a Brier of 0.221 against 0.052 in crypto (21 resolved) and 0.294 against 0.168 in economy (12 resolved). This strategy has lost $17 per $100 staked (22 bets, 6 settled). The experiment is to demand a bigger edge and skip Jev's worst categories, while leaving the info gate at 0.2 so it stays distinct from Jev alone.
proposals.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, P&L per $100 staked beats its all-time -$17.4 per $100 and is at least as good as jev_alone over the same period.
proposals.status_reason: jev_alone_bold rules v2: edge bar 8% → 12%; skips none → crypto, economy

proposals.title: Break results down by price paid
proposals.why: Many losses, including all 3 of claude_direct's and every info-gate-stopped group, show -$100 per $100, meaning the whole stake was lost. That pattern suggests we may be buying cheap longshots. A breakdown of wins and P&L by ask price (for example <0.2, 0.2–0.5, 0.5–0.8, >0.8), for placed and stopped bets, would let us set min_ask and max_ask from evidence instead of guessing.
proposals.judge_by: The review data includes a by-price breakdown, and within 2 reviews it leads to either a min_ask/max_ask tune or a clear finding that price doesn't matter.

proposals.title: Claude direct, pickier and without crypto
proposals.why: Claude is our best forecaster (Brier 0.132 on 24) yet lost all 3 of its settled bets. The places where it disagrees with the market by only 8% are probably where the market is right. This challenger demands a 12% edge, skips crypto, and bets half as much per bet.
proposals.judge_by: Positive P&L, and more P&L per $100 staked than claude_direct over the same period.
proposals.status_reason: started automatically within the allowed bounds

proposals.title: Bold meets the info gate halfway
proposals.why: Bold's extra bets, where Jev's info rating is 0.2–0.5, are losing $31.79 per $100 (7 bets), and main's info-stopped markets lose $70 per $100 (16). A 0.35 threshold tests where the cutoff really belongs, without collapsing bold into a copy of main.
proposals.judge_by: Bold's P&L per $100 staked since the change beats its old -$31.79 per $100, and is closer to or above main's over the same period.

proposals.title: Main skips crypto
proposals.why: In crypto the market scores a Brier of 0.034 against Jev+research's 0.117 (9 resolved), so any edge we think we see there is most likely our own error. This is an experiment on a small sample.
proposals.judge_by: On the yardstick, main's P&L on bets opened after this change is at least original's. Meanwhile, original's crypto bets over the same period lose money in total.
proposals.status_reason: main rules v2: skips none → crypto

retro.headline: A quiet half-day: nothing has settled since the 30c price floor went in on 2026-10-01, every strategy is still down, and none of the current rules can be changed for another four hours, so today is for watching rather than tuning.
went_well: Coin-flip prices (30-60c) are where main makes money: +$3,520 on 5 settled bets (3 wins). Original made +$1,136 on 4 bets in the same price range. That is 9 bets in total, so it is an experiment, not a finding, but it agrees with the reason for the price floor.

The info gate is stopping losers. Markets main skipped only because Jev said it lacked information would have lost $39.69 per $100 (62 markets). For Jev alone the figure is $45.54 per $100 (104 markets).
Calibrated is the closest to breaking even, at -$4,274. Both of its favourite bets (60c and up) won, for +$1,686, though that is only 2 bets.
went_badly: Every strategy is below $100k. Bold is worst at -$15,354 over 28 settled bets, then jev_alone_bold at -$13,408 and claude_direct at -$9,840 (0 wins in 5 settled). Most of those losses came from long shots placed before the floor.

The market is still the best forecaster. Its Brier score is 0.123 over 201 resolved markets (lower is better). Claude direct is close at 0.134, but only over 44. Jev + research scores 0.201 over 135 and Jev alone 0.244 over 201. The market's lead shows up in every category with real sample sizes: sp

Tuning main has not yet beaten original. On the bets both placed since original started, main is at -$4,983 and original at -$4,816 (7 settled each). That is a tie within noise, and no strategy has a single settled bet under its current rules.
